idiom_name: Playwright class wrapper: Locator fields + async service methods over Page
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the page object is a class that receives the framework's page object in its constructor, creates locator fields once and exposes async service methods - Playwright's POM guide shows exactly this shape, with auto-waiting locators that re-resolve on every action and web-first assertions left to the test. What replaces the classic Java-style structure is the framework's locator API plus ES modules: no base class and no reflection, so navigation methods can simply return the next page class. Tests import the class and construct it with the fixture's page.
pitfalls: Locators are lazy and survive navigation, but element handles (await page.$()) do not: a page object that stores handles goes stale after the first navigation.
Async methods must be awaited; an unawaited action resolves after the assertion and makes the failure appear in the next test.
Exporting a page-object instance instead of the class shares framework state across tests; in Playwright that fights per-test isolation (the singleton style belongs to WebdriverIO).

variants.name: WebdriverIO page objects: exported instances with lazy element getters
variants.idiom_name: WebdriverIO exported page instance with lazy $()/$$() getters
variants.implementation_notes: WebdriverIO was designed with the pattern in mind: a base Page class holds shared selectors and open(), each page exports a single instance (never constructed inside a test), and elements are exposed as getters - get username() { return $('#username') } - so the element command is created lazily on access and chaining works in the test (await LoginPage.username.setValue('max')). The elements-as-first-class-citizens principle and $/$$ chaining replace the classic field-and-proxy structure; the exported instance is safe because a page is treated as a stateless construct and state lives in the test or the browser session.
pitfalls: Getters create a fresh element command per access, but a stored element reference (or a value read from one) still points at the previous document after navigation.
Page objects should stay stateless: test-specific state on the exported singleton leaks between spec files.
Cypress-style frameworks recommend app actions and custom commands over shared page objects, so porting this style there fights the framework's isolation guidance.
